property_summary: After a Collect call, MinSum equals the value set by SetMinSum when called before initialization (reference), whereas the bug allows MinSum to be changed after initialization (buggy), so the rule is that MinSum is never greater than the value set before initialization.

After any sequence of operations ending with Collect, MinSum is always equal to the value it was set to when intitalized is false (before Initialize), and it never changes after intitalized becomes true.
After calling Collect with any amount, MinSum must remain unchanged (equal to its value before the call).
After any call to Collect, the value of MinSum must be at least the last value set by SetMinSum before Initialized was called.
The value of MinSum must never be changed by any call to Collect, regardless of inputs.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the MinSum state variable remains unchanged from its value after the last SetMinSum call before Initialized was called.

After any call to Collect, the MinSum state variable must still equal the value set by the last SetMinSum call before Initialized was called, or if Initialized was never called, it must equal the value set by the last SetMinSum call.
After any sequence of operations ending with a Collect call with a non-zero amount, MinSum should remain unchanged from its initial value if it was set before initialization.
After Collect succeeds (does not revert), MinSum must equal its value before Collect was called.
After any call to Collect(uint256), the unchanged public state variable MinSum should equal its value before the call.
After any call to Collect(uint256) with non-zero _am, the MinSum state variable remains equal to its value before the call.
After any call to Collect, the value of the public state variable MinSum remains unchanged from its value before the call.
After Collect is called, MinSum always equals its initial value (0) unless SetMinSum was previously called.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, MinSum equals the initial value (0) because SetMinSum can only be called once before initialization.

After any call to Collect, the value of MinSum is unchanged from its initial value (0) because SetMinSum can only be called before initialization, and the bug in the modifier does not affect that flow.
After any call to Collect, the balance of the caller decreases by the amount collected only if the call succeeds, and the invariant that MinSum remains unchanged from its initial value (0) holds.

After any sequence of calls ending with a call to Collect, the value of MinSum is equal to the last value set by SetMinSum, which can only be set before initialization; if SetMinSum was never called, MinSum remains 0.
After a successful Collect call that deducts balance, the Log contract's history length does not increase if Log was never set.
After Collect, the Log's HistoryLength is always at least as large as before the call.
Calling Collect never increases address(this).balance when SetLogFile was never called.
After any Collect call, the Log state variable (getter Log()) is unchanged.
After a Collect call that does not revert, Log state variable (address) is never changed from its initial zero value.
After calling Collect with any amount, the state variable Log remains unchanged in the reference but changes in the buggy version.
After Collect, the Log address stored in the contract equals the Log address before any external call.
After any call to Collect, the address stored in Log remains unchanged from its initial value.
After any sequence of permissible operations ending with Collect, the address stored in Log remains unchanged from its initial value set in the constructor.
After any call to Collect, the Log address stored in the contract is always zero (address(0)).
After calling Collect with any amount, the 'Initialized' function returns true if and only if Initialized() was called prior.
After a call to Collect, the Initialized state variable must remain false if Initialized() was never called.

After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, c.Initialized() returns the same value as before the sequence if no call to Initialized() was made, specifically it stays false when no call to Initialized() ever happens.
The state variable 'Initialized()' returns true after a call to Collect() only if Initialized() was explicitly called before.
The value of c.Initialized() is always false after any sequence of calls ending with Collect, if Initialized() was never called.
The balance of msg.sender after Collect must be at least the amount collected if the collect succeeds.
The balance of caller in mapping Acc after calling Collect is never incremented by the call's value when Collect does not revert.

After Collect() call, the caller's balance in Acc mapping is always less than or equal to their previous balance plus the amount collected, accounting for the mutated behavior where Put sets balance to msg.value instead of adding.
After a call to Collect(uint256) with a specific amount, the balance of the caller in the Acc mapping can never increase above the sum of their initial balance plus the amount collected.
After Collect, the caller's recorded balance in Acc cannot be greater than the sum of all values ever sent by that caller via Put (including fallback) minus amounts collected.
Collect should only succeed if the sender's unlockTime is in the past
The balance of the caller in Acc should stay the same if unlockTime is in the future at the time of collect.
After a Collect call, the caller's unlockTime in Acc should be strictly greater than the block timestamp at the time of the Put that last updated it, not equal or less.
After a Collect call, the caller's unlockTime in Acc should never be equal to the block timestamp, unless it was already strictly greater before the Put that set it.
After Collect, the caller's unlockTime in Acc must be strictly greater than the block timestamp at the time of the Put that last set it.
After Collect is called with any amount, the caller's balance in the contract should only decrease if the caller's unlockTime was in the past relative to block.timestamp.
After Collect is called, the caller's contract balance should only decrease if the caller's unlockTime is strictly less than block.timestamp.
After Collect(amount) reverts, the balance of the caller in the contract must not decrease when block.timestamp <= unlockTime.
After Collect is called, the caller's unlockTime does not increase.
After any Collect call, if the caller's lock time is in the future (block.timestamp <= unlockTime), the caller's contract balance should not decrease.
